ky_northern_gorge.blurb: The Northern Gorge is the part of Kentucky's Red River Gorge that lies north of the Mountain Parkway, inside the national forest and its wilderness land. The terrain is a heavily forested canyon system, so the cliffs tend to hide among the trees, and the climbing is on pocketed, often overhanging sandstone. Cliffs are mostly modest in height and scattered across dozens of separate walls and ridges rather than one big crag. Traditional climbing is the largest share, with a solid block of sport routes and a sizable number of boulder problems. Routes cluster between 5.8 and 5.12, with the heaviest concentration around 5.10, plus easier lines on most walls. Boulder problems are mostly V0 to V2. Walls such as Long Wall, Pistol Ridge, Military Wall and Fortress Wall carry the biggest counts.

tx_hueco_tanks.blurb: Hueco Tanks rises out of a high Chihuahuan Desert basin east of the Franklin Mountains, roughly 30 miles from El Paso. The rock is syenite, a relative of granite, and its surface is pocked with the water-holding basins that give the place its name; the huecos form holds, ledges and overhangs. This is a bouldering destination first: nearly everything here is a boulder problem, with a few roped trad, sport and top-rope lines on the side. Grades run from V0 up to the extreme end, with a deep spread of easy and middle problems and a long tail of hard ones. The climbing is divided among North Mountain, East Mountain, East Spur and West Mountain, and North Mountain holds the most problems. The climbing season generally runs from October through March.

ar_horseshoe_canyon_ranch.blurb: Horseshoe Canyon Ranch sits in north-central Arkansas along Highway 74, between Jasper and Ponca. The cliffs are fine-grained sandstone, and the walls are divided into four sections: the North Side, West Side and East Side hold nearly all of the climbing, while the Valley Floor is a small corner. Sport climbing makes up about half of the climbs, with a large number of boulder problems and a smaller helping of trad and crack climbs. Roped routes concentrate between 5.8 and 5.12 with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so there are plenty of moderates alongside the harder lines. Boulder problems skew easy to middling, from V0 through V5, with harder ones scattered above.

nv_red_rock_bouldering.blurb: Red Rock bouldering spreads across the sandstone canyons just west of Las Vegas, where the dramatic desert scenery comes with long, sun-baked days. Nearly all of it is bouldering, from V0 to the very hard, with the heaviest weight on V1 to V5 and a good supply of harder problems. Kraft Boulders is the biggest and best-known cluster, close to the road with short walks and a large collection of quality boulders in the single-digit grades. Gateway Canyon lies farther out and is known for harder problems. Red Spring, Willow Springs and Windy Canyon add more. Winter is the realistic season, because most boulders face south and shade is scarce, though a few canyons stay shaded for most of the day.

ca_high_sierra.blurb: The High Sierra stretches from the Sawtooth area in the north to the Whitney group in the south, a huge span of mostly wilderness built from granite. Most of the climbing is alpine in character: long ridges, buttresses and faces on high peaks, with a large share of scrambling and easy mountaineering, plus some trad, bouldering and a little ice. Rock routes run from easy fifth class through the 5.10 range, with the greatest number around 5.10 and a few harder lines. Whitney and its neighbors, Little Lakes Valley, Bishop Pass, the Palisades and the Sawtooth Ridge hold the most climbs. Altitude and afternoon thunderstorms matter. Climbing is generally possible from June to early October, with September often the most settled month.

ut_joe_s_valley.blurb: Joe's Valley is a high-desert bouldering area in Emery County, in central Utah, near Orangeville and Castle Dale. The rock is fine-grained sandstone with a grippy texture, and the climbing leans powerful and gymnastic, with overhangs, slopers and some technical face problems. Almost everything is a boulder problem, from V0 to the very hard, with a particularly good spread from V1 to V8 and a smaller group of hard ones above. Climbing is split among Left Fork, Right Fork and New Joe's; Left Fork holds many classics near the road, while New Joe's is the warmest zone and packed most densely with boulders. Fall is the best season and spring is also good, while summer is generally too hot. A few ice climbs exist in winter.
